check: how much heap the full GameTest run needs, and what to pass
mechanism: build.gradle adds -Xmx only when -PgreatwallTestHeap is supplied; the property is optional, and its format is validated as a size such as 1024m.
evidenceFromHistory: The historical full run that included the whole GameTest suite, full-package-20261004, passed with -PgreatwallTestHeap=1024m. Its recorded command reads: gradlew --offline --dependency-verification=strict build runGameTest compileServerSmokeJava compileClientSmokeJava ... -PgreatwallTestHeap=1024m. So one gigabyte sufficed for 119 tests plus a full build.

defaultIfOmitted.source: java -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal, showing MaxHeapSize as ergonomic at roughly a quarter of physical memory

decision: Run without the property, so the GameTest JVM takes the 8 GB ergonomic default.
reasoning: It is eight times what the historical run needed, so it is not the binding constraint.
The profile finishes before this runs, so its 8.5 GB is released and physical memory is not contended; 31.9 GB total.
If the run does fail, passing an explicit smaller heap is the available lever for narrowing it, which is easier to reason about from a working baseline.
caveatWorthKeeping: Running without the property means no -Xmx appears on the command line at all, so any future reader comparing commands will not see a heap setting. That is deliberate rather than an omission.
